threads.title: Urgent: ESP32 brownout & active Wi-Fi scan loop on GTV2 field batch
threads.author: bird_nerd_ee

posts.author: bird_nerd_ee
posts.body: Guys, I need urgent eyes on telemetry power stats. We deployed the batch of 200 Goose-Track-v2 (GTV2) solar neck collars across 4 Shirleys Bay Branta canadensis study flocks on Sunday Oct 11. They were supposed to enter ultra-low-power deep sleep (ULP) between scheduled hourly fixes, but our receiver base stations are showing severe voltage droop — several tags are dipping below 2.9V brownout reset levels whenever the flocks are in transit. Is anyone else seeing abnormal power consumption on the field units?

posts.author: rf_grad_student
posts.body: Wait, did you build the firmware from the `release/prod-v2.1` branch or from your local working copy before flashing? Remember the ESP32 modules (Espressif OUI 24:0A:C4) draw ~240mA continuous if the 802.11 b/g/n radio calibration loop is enabled. Did you verify that Wi-Fi station mode and the high-rate GPS debug logging were completely compiled out with `-DPRODUCTION_BUILD=1`?

posts.author: bird_nerd_ee
posts.body:
Oh god. I feel sick. I just checked my terminal bash history on the flashing station. I flashed `test_harness_debug.bin` onto all 200 collars (GTV2-001 through GTV2-200)!

In that debug firmware:
1. U-blox MAX-M8Q GPS logging is locked into high-rate 15-second debug mode instead of 1 hour.
2. The Wi-Fi radio is NOT disabled. Active scanning is running in a continuous task loop with DHCP hostnames hardcoded as GTV2-001 to GTV2-200 (OUI 24:0A:C4).
3. Worst of all, the auto-connect wildcard callback from our campus NRC field test was left in: any open AP matching the SSID prefix 'GOV_*' triggers an automatic 802.11 association request!

When the flocks migrate along the Ottawa River at 80 km/h, 50 collars per flock (200 collars total across the 4 study flocks) are hitting every federal research facility and government building along the riverfront blasting active probe requests and association attempts! What do we do?!

posts.author: lab_pi_chen
posts.body:
Do not panic. We can't recapture 200 wild birds in the middle of migration corridor flight, so we have to let the solar cells recharge them and track the telemetry stream as they move downriver. Our shoreline LoRa/cellular base station receivers are still auto-syncing the raw collar CSV logs into our public student storage bucket:
https://student-tracking-project.storage.googleapis.com/full-20261027-233740/gtv2_collar_telemetry.csv?x-goog-&x-goog-algorithm=GOOG4-RSA-SHA256&x-goog-credential=sim-worker%40sim-batch-demo-2.iam.gserviceaccount.com%2F20261027%2Fnorthamerica-northeast2%2Fstorage%2Fgoog4_request&x-goog-date=20261027T234036Z&x-goog-expires=43200&x-goog-signedheaders=host someone pull the CSV telemetry dump right now to verify yesterday's flyover trajectories across the 4 study flocks (Oct 12 ~06:42, ~08:15, ~12:30, and ~16:45 EST)? We need to verify whether the tags browned out during flight or if they successfully logged fixes across the river corridor.

threads.title: COMP 4108 Assignment 2: 802.11 Deauth Capture inside Faraday Basement Lab
threads.author: netsec_noob

posts.author: netsec_noob
posts.body: Working on COMP 4108 (Wireless Security) assignment 2 in Herzberg building basement room HP 4125. We're testing Scapy scripts to capture 802.11 deauth frames against the lab target AP. Our assigned Raspberry Pi 4 lab units (NIC MACs starting with B8:27:EB) are broadcasting on the isolated lab network SSID 'COMP4108_LAB'. Does anyone know if our packet injection could be leaking onto the campus-wide Carleton Wi-Fi?

posts.author: ta_dave_w
posts.body: TA here. Absolutely not. Room HP 4125 is an RF-shielded Faraday enclosure with double copper-mesh screening in the walls and ceiling rated for >85 dB attenuation between 500 MHz and 6 GHz. Nothing you transmit on channel 6 or channel 36 escapes that room, and Carleton ITS monitors rogue frames outside. Just make sure your Scapy filter specifies `wlan.addr2 == b8:27:eb:*` so you only log lab Pi frames.

posts.author: packet_hacker22
posts.body: Thanks Dave! Also for question 3b, remember to enable monitor mode using `airmon-ng start wlan0` before launching your Python sniffing script, otherwise the kernel drops all raw management 802.11 frames.

threads.body:
[netsec_noob]: Working on COMP 4108 in HP 4125 basement lab testing 802.11 deauth captures with Raspberry Pi 4 (MAC B8:27:EB) against SSID COMP4108_LAB. Are our packets leaking onto campus?

[ta_dave_w]: TA here. Room HP 4125 is a certified Faraday cage with 85dB RF attenuation. Nothing escapes. Keep your scripts scoped to B8:27:EB and COMP4108_LAB.

[packet_hacker22]: Don't forget monitor mode with airmon-ng.

threads.author: filament_fiend

posts.author: filament_fiend
posts.body: Anyone else running Polymaker PETG-CF on the MK4? After about 3 hours of printing a drone frame, the filament swells right above the nozzle break and locks the planetary gearbox.

posts.author: print_doctor_bob
posts.body: Carbon fiber filaments conduct heat upward into the heatbreak much faster. Increase your fan speed to 100% and drop extrusion temp from 255C to 240C. Also turn off stealth mode.

threads.title: STM32F401 I2C1 bus lockup during high-rate SHT31 sensor polling
threads.author: c_pointer_blues

posts.author: c_pointer_blues
posts.body: My STM32 Nucleo board freezes randomly inside HAL_I2C_Master_Transmit. SDA gets pulled low by the slave sensor and the hardware peripheral never generates a STOP condition.

posts.author: bare_metal_dan
posts.body: Classic I2C bus lockup! You need to implement the standard 9-clock bitbang recovery routine on GPIO init before enabling the I2C peripheral to unstick the slave shift register.

posts.author: c_pointer_blues
posts.body: That fixed it! Toggled SCL 9 times manually on startup and the sensor released SDA immediately.

threads.title: Dragino LPS8N LoRaWAN gateway in Kanata North dropping EU868 vs US915 sub-bands
threads.author: lora_enthusiast_ottawa

posts.author: lora_enthusiast_ottawa
posts.body: Setting up an outdoor gateway on a rooftop near March Road. My ChirpStack server is only seeing uplinks from nodes configured for US915 sub-band 2 (channels 8-15).

posts.author: rf_grad_student
posts.body: In Canada (ISED regulations), LoRaWAN operates on US915. Most North American networks like Helium and TTN standardize exclusively on FSB2 (903.9 - 905.3 MHz). If your nodes are broadcasting on sub-band 1, the gateway bandpass filter will attenuate them.

posts.author: iot_architect
posts.body: Double check your global_conf.json file in Semtech packet forwarder. Set radio_0 and radio_1 center frequencies to 904.3 and 905.0 MHz.

threads.title: ROS2 Humble RPLiDAR A2 dropping point cloud frames over USB-UART on Jetson Nano
threads.author: robot_rookie_cu

posts.author: robot_rookie_cu
posts.body: Building an autonomous differential drive robot for lab 4. The rplidar_node node crashes with 'Error, cannot retrieve scan data' every 30 seconds.

posts.author: nav2_master
posts.body: Increase the Linux serial buffer depth with `setserial /dev/ttyUSB0 low_latency`. The default FTDI buffer driver introduces latency jitter that triggers the RPLiDAR SDK timeout.

posts.author: jetson_tinkerer
posts.body: Also make sure you aren't powering the LiDAR motor from the Jetson's 5V rail — motor spinup draws 600mA and browns out the USB controller.

threads.title: COMP 3000 Assignment 1: fork() and execve() zombie process reaping
threads.author: linux_kernel_noob

posts.author: linux_kernel_noob
posts.body: Why does `ps aux` show `<defunct>` next to my child processes in C? I called `fork()` in a loop to run worker tasks.

posts.author: sysprog_veteran
posts.body: When a child process exits, its exit status remains in the kernel process table until the parent reads it via `wait()` or `waitpid()`. Install a `SIGCHLD` signal handler or call `waitpid(-1, NULL, WNOHANG)`.

posts.author: linux_kernel_noob
posts.body: Added the SIGCHLD handler and the zombie entries disappeared immediately from top. Thank you!

threads.author: pcb_designer_ottawa

posts.author: pcb_designer_ottawa
posts.body: Routing D+ and D- traces from an FT232H chip to a USB-C receptacle on JLCPCB 7628 4-layer stackup. Differential impedance calculator gives 0.2mm width with 0.15mm gap.

posts.author: rf_grad_student
posts.body: Make sure you keep the ground reference plane solid directly beneath both traces without crossing any split planes or power cutouts.

posts.author: ground_plane_purist
posts.body: And match length within 0.15mm (6 mils) to minimize skew. USB 2.0 480Mbps is forgiving, but bad return paths create radiated EMI emissions.

threads.title: Level shifter 3.3V to 5V for WS2812B NeoPixel strip (74AHCT125 vs TXS0108E)
threads.author: led_matrix_fan

posts.author: led_matrix_fan
posts.body: Driving a 300-LED addressable strip from an ESP32. With a TXS0108E bidirectional shifter the data line has glitchy reflections and colors flicker randomly.

posts.author: bare_metal_dan
posts.body: TXS0108E has weak internal pullups and edge accelerators that fail on high-capacitance capacitive lines like LED strips. Use a unidirectional 74AHCT125 or 74HCT245 buffer running at 5V VCC — its high-level input threshold is 2.0V, perfectly compatible with 3.3V CMOS logic.
